correctness.rationale: The graph incidence identity AA^T=A^T A=(k−lambda)I+lambda J gives an explicit inverse of the bipartite graph Laplacian on the zero-mean vertex subspaces; the constant/anti-constant eigenvectors are handled separately. This yields an exact closed transfer-current kernel for every pair of edges, not an approximation. Counting the two shared-endpoint and three disjoint crossing classes using the design axioms yields five exact nonnegative counts. Only the one-cross and two-cross entries are negative. Because the all-ones edge flow is a gradient, the absolute row sum equals one plus twice the negative mass, proving the gradient norm. The diagonal equals (2v−1)/(vk), proving the circulation norm; their difference (k−4)/k+2/(vk) gives the strict degree transition. Sign vectors attain each induced infinity norm. An independently coded exact grounded-Laplacian solve passed 5,979 assertions in nine test designs; these computations are checks, while the full-parameter claim is proved analytically.

value.rationale: The quantity controls worst-case coordinatewise amplification when irregular edge observations are orthogonally fitted to potential differences or circulation residuals, a standard sharp robustness invariant. Symmetric block designs form a naturally parameterized family of connected bipartite networks for which transitivity need not hold. An exact five-class transfer-current law unexpectedly makes both stability constants depend only on the design parameters and yields a uniform crossover at block size four, separating the gradient and cycle instabilities. The finite equality witnesses and asymptotic projective-plane families demonstrate operative, not merely formal, bounds. Neither routine nonexpansivity in the Hilbert norm nor a general electrical-flow bound yields the exact infinity norms. No unproved downstream application is needed for this value claim.
